summary: sync rewrites the whole ledger from a snapshot it read many seconds earlier, with no lock and no re-read before mv. Any write that lands during the run (annotate-pr, resolve, defer, a concurrent archive) is silently reverted, and archived entries come back.
failure_scenario: Setup: the statusline autosync (list-status.sh:177) or SessionStart sync begins a pass on a ledger with PR-annotated entries. Each entry costs a gh network call plus about 65 forks, so the pass takes tens of seconds. Meanwhile the post-bash hook runs `annotate-pr` after `gh pr create` (post-bash-dispatch.sh:249), or the agent runs `resolve` or `defer`. Each of those does its own tmp+mv. The sync loop is still reading the OLD inode through its open fd. When it finishes, `mv "$tmp" "$file"` overwrites the newer file, so the annotation, resolve or defer is gone with no message. The entry then never closes on merge. Second case: an explicit `sync` finishes its auto-archive (entries moved to the archive file) while a slower unattended sync that began earlier is still running. The slow sync then mv's its pre-archive snapshot back, so the archived entries reappear in the active ledger. The next archive pass appends them to the archive a second time, giving duplicates. The no-op path is also affected: `mv` runs even when nothing changed, so every sync, including the idle ones, opens this window. The post-bash-dispatch.sh header (lines 14-23) claims ordering avoids the race. That only covers the one sync it spawns, not an already-running one.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:93 tmp="$(mktemp -t found-issues.XXXXXX)"; lib/sync.sh:100 while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do ... lib/sync.sh:361 done <"$file"; lib/sync.sh:367 mv "$tmp" "$file" (reached unconditionally when not dry-run); lib/resolve.sh:153 mv "$tmp" "$file" (the same unserialized read-modify-write pattern in every mutator)
suggested_fix: Serialize every ledger mutator with an atomic `mkdir "$file.lock"` lock that has stale-PID cleanup, since mkdir is portable to bash 3.2 and Git Bash. Better, make sync two-phase: decide closures and renames outside the lock, then take the lock, re-read the current file, apply each decision by exact-line match, and write only if something changed.
needs_runtime_repro: Build a ledger with 1 entry annotated (PR: o/r#1) and a stub `gh` on PATH that sleeps 5s. Run `found-issues sync &`. After 1s run `found-issues log docs/a.md:1 — new issue`, or `resolve` an unrelated entry. After `wait`, check that docs/found-issues.md has lost the logged or resolved change.

summary: The tmp file is created with `mktemp -t` in $TMPDIR, not next to the ledger. When $TMPDIR and the repo are on different filesystems, `mv` is a non-atomic copy+unlink, so the 'atomic tmp+mv' assumption in the code and hook comments is false. The mv also replaces the ledger's file mode with 0600.
failure_scenario: Linux with /tmp on tmpfs and the repo on ext4 or a Docker bind mount, or Windows Git Bash with TEMP on C: and the repo on D:. `mv "$tmp" "$file"` becomes copy+unlink. A statusline render, `log` append or another sync reading mid-copy sees a truncated ledger. A crash or ENOSPC mid-copy leaves a truncated ledger, with every entry after the cut lost. Separately, mktemp creates 0600, so a 0644 ledger becomes 0600 after the first sync or resolve. A second Unix user or a container user then loses read access, and a symlinked ledger is replaced by a regular file.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:93 mktemp -t found-issues.XXXXXX; lib/sync.sh:367 mv "$tmp" "$file"; lib/archive.sh:139 mktemp -t found-issues-archive.XXXXXX and :150 mv "$tmp" "$file"; lib/resolve.sh:139/:153; lib/parse-entries.sh:684/:738 and :785/:839; lib/annotate.sh:150/:173 and :529/:542
suggested_fix: Create the tmp in the ledger's directory (`mktemp "$file.tmp.XXXXXX"`) so rename(2) is atomic. Copy the original mode onto it before mv, for example via `[ -r ] && chmod` with a portable stat helper such as fi_file_mtime's GNU/BSD pattern. Put the tmp pattern in .gitignore or clean it on EXIT.
needs_runtime_repro: On Linux run `TMPDIR=/dev/shm found-issues resolve <match>` against a repo on a normal disk, with `strace -f -e trace=rename,renameat2,unlink` attached. Observe rename failing with EXDEV followed by copy and unlink. Also compare `stat -c %a docs/found-issues.md` before and after the run.

summary: The active ledger is rewritten with `grep -F -x -v -f ... > tmp || true` and then mv'd over the original with no check of grep's exit status or of the output size. If grep errors or treats the ledger as binary, the ledger is replaced by an empty or partial file.
failure_scenario: A ledger that contains any line with invalid UTF-8 bytes, or a NUL, is read by GNU grep in a UTF-8 locale as a binary file. This can happen when a symptom was byte-truncated mid-character by some tool. In `-v` mode grep then suppresses line output. Depending on version it prints 'Binary file ... matches' to stdout, which lands in tmp, or it prints nothing. The `|| true` hides exit 2, so `mv "$tmp" "$file"` replaces the ledger with that message or an empty file. Only the archived lines survive, in the archive file. Every [open] and [deferred] entry is lost. The same destruction follows any other grep failure, such as ENOSPC or an unreadable pattern file. parse-entries.sh:51 already uses `LC_ALL=C grep` for this class of problem, but archive.sh does not.
evidence: lib/archive.sh:148 grep -F -x -v -f "$patterns_file" "$file" >"$tmp" || true; lib/archive.sh:150 mv "$tmp" "$file" (no status or line-count check between them)
suggested_fix: Run grep as `LC_ALL=C grep -a -F -x -v -f ...` and treat exit status >1 as fatal (abort before mv). Before mv, assert the tmp line count equals the original minus archived_count. Alternatively do the removal in awk with an exact-line set, which has no binary-file mode.
needs_runtime_repro: Create docs/found-issues.md with one `- [fixed] 2020-01-01 a.sh:1 — old (fixed: 2020-01-02)` line plus one `- [open] 2026-10-01 b.sh:1 — bad $'\xff' byte` line. Run `LANG=en_US.UTF-8 found-issues archive` with GNU grep. Check whether the [open] line survived in docs/found-issues.md.

summary: The archive awk depends on regex interval expressions `{4}`, `{2}`. Some mawk builds that are the default `awk` on stock Debian and Ubuntu treat braces literally. Those builds never match a date, so archive reports 'nothing to archive' forever.
failure_scenario: On Debian 11/12 and Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 without gawk installed, `awk` is mawk 1.3.4-20200120, where repetitions are not enabled by default. `match(line, /\(fixed: [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\)/)` and the header-date fallback at :71 never match. `fixed_pairs` stays empty, `fixed_total` is 0, and archive prints 'nothing to archive / fixed entries: 0'. Auto-archive and `--days` never move anything on those hosts, so the ledger grows without bound, silently and with a plausible message.
evidence: lib/archive.sh:69 if (match(line, /\(fixed: [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\)/)) {; lib/archive.sh:71 } else if (match(line, / [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} /)) {; lib/archive.sh:112 printf '  fixed entries: %d (threshold: %d)\n' (reports 0)
suggested_fix: Avoid intervals in awk. Use `[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]`, or extract the date with the bash `[[ =~ ]]` regex already used elsewhere. Add a bats case that runs with mawk.
needs_runtime_repro: On a host with mawk: `printf -- '- [fixed] 2020-01-01 a — b (fixed: 2020-01-02)\n' | mawk '/^- \[fixed\]/ { print match($0, /\(fixed: [0-9]{4}-/) }'` prints 0. Then run `found-issues archive --days 1` on a ledger with an old [fixed] line and see 'nothing to archive'.

summary: Process creations per [open] entry in sync, about 65 forks with 40 execs for a plain entry whose file exists, and about 75 with one PR annotation. All of it is avoidable with builtins or hoisting.
failure_scenario: Per entry, with file:line for each source. (1) parse-entries.sh:109 `$(printf|sed)` is 3 forks. (2) :199 `$(fi_annotation_tail)` is 1 fork. (3) :203-206, :215-218, :222-225, :229-232, :237-240 and :244-247 are six `$(printf|grep -oE|sed|paste)` pipelines at 5 forks each, so 30 forks and 18 execs. (4) sync.sh:106 wraps fi_parse_entry in `$()`, 1 fork. (5) sync.sh:107-112 are five `$(printf|grep|head -1|cut)` at 5 forks each, so 25 forks and 15 execs, re-splitting a string the parser just built. (6) sync.sh:239 `repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel || pwd)` runs per entry although the value is loop-invariant, 2 forks. (7) sync.sh:254-259 computes recovered_loc via `$(printf|sed)`, 3 forks. The guard `e_path != *[[:space:]]*` at :254 is always true because e_path is the first token, so this runs for every entry with `/` or `.` in the path even when the file exists. Only the missing-path branch needs it. (8) Per PR annotation, sync.sh:164, :165 and :175 each run `$(printf|jq)`, 3 forks apiece, plus the gh call itself. On Windows Git Bash each of these is a Windows process creation and a possible kernel-token leak. SessionStart runs sync synchronously (session-start.sh:366), so this cost is paid on every session.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:107 e_path="$(printf '%s' "$e_data" | grep '^path=' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-)" (repeated at :108,:109,:111,:112); lib/sync.sh:239 repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"; lib/sync.sh:255 recovered_loc="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed -E ...)"; lib/parse-entries.sh:203-206 prs="$(printf '%s' "$ann_tail" | grep -oE ... | sed -E ... | paste -sd , - ...)" (x6); lib/parse-entries.sh:585-607 already has a zero-fork `while read; case ${kv%%=*}` parser in fi_entry_to_json
suggested_fix: Add a builtin `fi_parse_entry_vars` that sets globals. Walk ann_tail with `while [[ $rest =~ \(PR: (...)\) ]]` plus BASH_REMATCH to build the comma lists, and have fi_parse_entry print from it. In sync, call it directly and drop :106-112 (or reuse the :585 read loop). Hoist repo_root above the loop. Move recovered_loc inside `[[ ! -e "$full_path" ]]` and compute it with parameter expansion. Add a builtin pre-filter like annotate.sh:391-412: entries with no `(PR:`/`(commit:`/`-auto:` token and an existing path need no forks. Replace the three jq calls with one `gh pr view --json state,baseRefName,mergedAt --jq '[.state,.baseRefName,.mergedAt]|@tsv'` split via `read`.
needs_runtime_repro: Run `strace -f -c -e trace=execve found-issues sync --dry-run` on a ledger with N plain open entries and compare against N+10 entries. The delta divided by 10 gives execs per entry, which should be about 40.

summary: For every [open] entry whose path is absent from disk, sync runs a whole-history `git log --diff-filter=R -M --name-status` (plus 2 awk) up to twice, before checking whether git ever tracked the path. Abstract locations such as `workflow/release-process` are never tombstoned, so they pay this on every sync forever.
failure_scenario: The ledger holds K entries with abstract locations containing `/` or `.` (the code at :237 treats them as file-like), for example 'workflow/release-process' or 'node.js'. Each sync, which means every SessionStart, every 10-minute autosync and every post-merge hook, runs fi_detect_rename up to 2K times (recovered_loc and e_path). Each call walks the full history with rename detection, then runs a pure-bash O(renames x hops) chain loop. fi_git_confirms_removed then runs `git log -1 -- path`. On a 50k-commit repo each rename scan costs seconds. Since the entry can never close, the cost is never amortized, and the SessionStart hook has no timeout (session-start.sh:366).
evidence: lib/sync.sh:286-291 `detected_new_path="$(cd "$repo_root" && fi_detect_rename "$recovered_loc")"` ... `elif detected_new_path="$(cd "$repo_root" && fi_detect_rename "$e_path")"`; bin/found-issues:182 renames="$(git log --diff-filter=R -M --name-status --pretty=format: 2>/dev/null | awk ...)"; bin/found-issues:196-209 per-call chain loop; bin/found-issues:165 the cheap `git log -1 --pretty=format:%H -- "$path"` check only runs afterwards
suggested_fix: Gate both rename and tombstone on the cheap path-indexed check first: if `git log -1 --format=%H -- "$path"` is empty, the path was never tracked, so no rename or removal is possible. Compute `renames` once per sync in a lazily set global instead of per call.
needs_runtime_repro: In a repo with a few thousand commits, add 5 entries like `- [open] 2026-10-01 workflow/release-process — x`. Run `time found-issues sync --dry-run`, and compare with `GIT_TRACE=1` showing the repeated `git log --diff-filter=R` runs.

summary: Every PR closure path is gated on `command -v jq`, but the gh calls could use gh's built-in `--jq`. On a machine with gh and no jq (the Git Bash default), PR-annotated entries never close and sync says nothing.
failure_scenario: Windows Git Bash has gh but no jq. For an entry annotated (PR: o/r#9) whose PR merged, the whole block at :148 is skipped. No gh_empty_warnings entry is recorded, because that list is filled only inside the block. sync prints 'Synced. Nothing to close.' and the entry stays [open] indefinitely. The same gate on :133 hides awaiting-confirmation reports.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:148 if [[ -n "$e_prs" && -n "$repo_id" ]] && command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then; lib/sync.sh:139 already uses gh's own `--jq '.state // empty'`
suggested_fix: Drop the jq requirement: fetch state, baseRefName and mergedAt through gh `--jq` as @tsv. If gh is missing and PR annotations exist, emit a one-line warning so the skip is visible.
needs_runtime_repro: Run with a PATH that has gh but no jq, on a ledger entry annotated with a merged PR. The entry stays [open] and no warning appears.

summary: Network and gh calls have no memoization or short-circuit. `gh auth status` runs before the mode cache is consulted. `gh pr view` runs once per annotated entry per sync, with no per-run dedupe and no TTL. The default-branch lookup is uncached when gh fails.
failure_scenario: (a) detect-mode.sh:90 `gh auth status` runs before the 1h mode-cache check at :106, so every sync, and every log/resolve/defer through fi_resolve_issues_file (bin/found-issues:221), pays a gh round trip. In sync, mode is only used to gate repo_id (sync.sh:70). (b) sync.sh:156 and :139 run `gh pr view` per entry per sync. Entries sharing one PR query it repeatedly, and still-open PRs are re-queried at every SessionStart, autosync and post-merge sync. (c) bin/found-issues:312 `gh repo view` has no negative cache. With a GitHub remote and no origin/HEAD, an offline or failing gh retries the network call on every sync. All of this sits on the synchronous SessionStart path with no timeout.
evidence: lib/detect-mode.sh:90 if ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then (cache check only at :106); lib/sync.sh:156 pr_json="$(gh pr view "$pr_num" --repo "$pr_repo" --json state,baseRefName,mergedAt,isDraft 2>/dev/null || true)"; bin/found-issues:312 gh_result="$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef ...)"
suggested_fix: Check the mode cache before `gh auth status`. Memoize `gh pr view` per `repo#N` within one sync using a newline-delimited string (no associative arrays on bash 3.2). Write a short negative-cache stamp when the default-branch lookup fails. Consider a hard timeout on the SessionStart sync.
needs_runtime_repro: With a stub gh on PATH that logs argv, run `found-issues sync` on a ledger with 3 entries sharing one open PR. Expect 3 `pr view` calls plus 1 `auth status` per run.

summary: The statusline autosync spawns `sync` with no cwd or --cwd, but cmd_sync ignores --cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and searches the ledger from $PWD only. The throttle stamp is also global, not per ledger.
failure_scenario: cmd_status finds the ledger through `--cwd` or CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. The in-code comment at :90-98 and docs/configuration.md say the statusline subprocess does not inherit the workspace as cwd. The detached `"$0" sync` therefore runs with the statusline's own $PWD, for example $HOME. cmd_sync calls `fi_find_issues_file` with no argument, which fails with 'sync: no found-issues.md found' (exit 1, output sent to /dev/null). Autosync is then a silent no-op, and PR merges only flip at the next SessionStart. If $HOME or an ancestor holds a ledger, sync would instead mutate that unrelated ledger. The stamp file `segment-autosync-ts` is global across repos, so with 3-5 parallel sessions in different repos, whichever renders first after 600s claims the slot and the others skip.
evidence: lib/list-status.sh:177 ( FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off "$0" sync >/dev/null 2>&1 & ) >/dev/null 2>&1; lib/sync.sh:61 file="$(fi_find_issues_file)" || {; lib/parse-entries.sh:23 local start="${1:-$PWD}"; lib/list-status.sh:146 _autosync_ts="$_autosync_cache/segment-autosync-ts"
suggested_fix: Pass the resolved search root to the child (`( cd "$(dirname "$file")" && ... sync )`), or give sync a `--cwd` honoring CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR the way status does. Key the throttle stamp by ledger path.
needs_runtime_repro: Run `cd "$HOME" && CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/path/to/repo found-issues sync`. Expect 'sync: no found-issues.md found' and exit 1 even though status --cwd finds the ledger. Then trigger `status --format=segment --cwd /repo` with a due stamp and check whether the ledger changes.

summary: fi_resolve_default_branch falls back to the literal 'main' without checking the branch exists. On a repo whose default is master or trunk and which has no origin/HEAD and no usable gh, PR and commit closure silently never fires.
failure_scenario: A repo made with `git init` + `git remote add` + push (origin/HEAD unset), or a non-GitHub remote, or gh offline, with default branch `master`. default_branch becomes 'main'. For a merged PR, `pr_branch` ('master') != 'main', so sync.sh:166 never closes it. For commits, both `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main` calls fail with 'not a valid object name' and the stderr is discarded (sync.sh:190-191). Entries stay [open] forever and nothing is reported.
evidence: bin/found-issues:321-323 `# Last resort` printf 'main'; return 0; lib/sync.sh:166 [[ "$pr_state" == "MERGED" && ( -z "$default_branch" || "$pr_branch" == "$default_branch" ) ]]; lib/sync.sh:190-191 the two is-ancestor probes with 2>/dev/null
suggested_fix: Verify the fallback with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/main refs/remotes/origin/main`, then try master, trunk and `init.defaultBranch`. If none resolve, return empty and have sync print a one-line 'default branch unresolved, closures skipped' notice.
needs_runtime_repro: git init with branch master, add a fake github.com origin, no origin/HEAD, gh absent from PATH. Annotate an entry with a commit that is on master, run sync, and confirm it is not closed.

summary: A (commit: sha) annotation whose SHA does not resolve locally is demoted to (commit-stale:) permanently. 'Does not resolve' also happens in shallow or partial clones, on a machine that has not fetched the branch, or for an ambiguous 7-hex SHA, not only after squash or force-push.
failure_scenario: Another machine, a CI checkout with depth 1, or a clone that has not fetched the fix branch runs sync on a ledger carrying `(commit: abc1234)`. `git rev-parse --verify abc1234` fails (not fetched, or 'short object ID is ambiguous'). The line is rewritten to `(commit-stale: abc1234)`, and that edit is committed with the ledger. `commits` extraction (parse-entries.sh:229) only reads `(commit: `, so when the commit later lands on the default branch the entry never closes. The demotion is not reversed by any command.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:189 if git rev-parse --verify "$sha" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... :198-200 else demote_commit_refs+=("$sha"); lib/sync.sh:350 demoted_line="${demoted_line//(commit: $ref)/(commit-stale: $ref)}"
suggested_fix: Demote only when the repo is complete (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is false and the ref lookup is not an ambiguity error), or only after the SHA has failed on two syncs. Otherwise leave the annotation and warn.
needs_runtime_repro: Run `git clone --depth 1 file://$PWD /tmp/shallow` on a repo whose ledger has `(commit: <old sha>)`, then run `found-issues sync --dry-run` in the shallow clone. Expect 'Demoted: 1 (0 PR-closed + 1 commit-stale)'.

summary: Rename detection parses `git log --name-status` without `-z` or quotepath=off, so non-ASCII paths arrive C-quoted and never match. A renamed file then falls through to the tombstone branch and the entry is closed as 'removed'.
failure_scenario: An entry cites `docs/café.md:3` and the file is `git mv`d to `docs/cafe.md`. name-status prints `R100\t"docs/caf\303\251.md"\tdocs/cafe.md`. The `$src == $current` comparison fails, so rename detection returns 1. fi_git_confirms_removed then finds the path absent from HEAD with history, and sync.sh:306-308 closes the live entry with `(closure: tombstone)`. The closure is irreversible.
evidence: bin/found-issues:182 git log --diff-filter=R -M --name-status --pretty=format: 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '/^R[0-9]+\t/ { print $2 "\t" $3 }'; lib/sync.sh:299-309 fallback to tombstone when no rename matched
suggested_fix: Use `git -c core.quotepath=off log ... -z` (and split on NUL), or `-c core.quotepath=off` at minimum. If the path contains non-ASCII bytes and detection is inconclusive, decline to tombstone.
needs_runtime_repro: In a scratch repo: create docs/café.md, commit, `git mv docs/café.md docs/cafe.md`, commit. Add `- [open] 2026-10-01 docs/café.md:1 — x` to the ledger and run `found-issues sync`. The entry is tombstoned instead of renamed.

summary: The rename rewrite uses an unquoted pattern and an unquoted replacement in `${var/pat/repl}`. Glob characters in the pattern change what matches, and in bash 5.2 an `&` in the replacement is expanded to the matched text.
failure_scenario: A file renamed to a target containing `&`, for example `docs/R&D.md`. On bash >= 5.2 (patsub_replacement on by default), `${corrected_line/$rename_source/$rename_target}` turns the `&` into the old path, writing a garbled path into the ledger. The entry is then left [open] with a wrong location and a (renamed-from:) trail. The unquoted `$rename_source` is also treated as a glob. The e_path guard at :222 does not cover a recovered_loc that contains brackets.
suggested_fix: Quote both operands (`"$rename_source"`, `"$rename_target"`), and use a prefix/suffix split instead of substitution so `&` is never special.
needs_runtime_repro: Under bash 5.2: `l='- [open] d a.md:1 — x'; s='a.md'; t='R&D.md'; echo "${l/$s/$t}"` shows the substitution corruption. Then reproduce end to end with a git mv to a name containing &.

summary: On a CRLF ledger (Git for Windows with autocrlf), closing an entry appends the closure label after the line's trailing CR, leaving a lone CR in the middle of the line.
failure_scenario:
A ledger line `...text` read with `read -r` keeps its . `printf '%s %s
' "$fixed_line" "$closure_label"` writes `...text (fixed: 2026-10-03)
`. The other lines keep CRLF and this one ends in LF. git's autocrlf normalizes only CRLF pairs, so the stray CR is committed and later rendered as ` (fixed...)
`. This produces diff noise and a mid-line control character.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:327-328 fixed_line="${line/\[open\]/[fixed]}"; printf '%s %s\n' "$fixed_line" "$closure_label" >>"$tmp"; same pattern in lib/resolve.sh:147 and lib/annotate.sh:164/:534
suggested_fix: Strip a trailing CR before appending (`line_nocr=${line%$'\r'}`), then re-append it after the new text when the original line had one.
needs_runtime_repro: Convert docs/found-issues.md to CRLF with unix2dos, close an entry via a merged PR or tombstone, and run `grep -c $'\r (fixed' docs/found-issues.md`.

summary: archive's line identity is not preserved: `IFS=$'\t' read -r date line` strips trailing tabs, and `grep -x -v` removes every identical line, not just the archived one. The result is a perpetually duplicated archive entry or a silently deleted duplicate.
failure_scenario: (a) A [fixed] line ending in a tab: `read` strips it, so the archived text differs from the active line. `grep -F -x -v` no longer matches the active line, so the entry is appended to the archive again on every archive run while staying in the active ledger. (b) Two byte-identical old [fixed] lines where the count rule (not the date rule) selects only one: the :148 pattern file removes both active copies, but only one was archived, so one entry is lost.
evidence: lib/archive.sh:95 while IFS=$'\t' read -r date line; do; lib/archive.sh:103 to_archive_lines+="$line"$'\n'; lib/archive.sh:148 grep -F -x -v -f "$patterns_file" "$file"
suggested_fix: Rewrite by line number (awk with an explicit set of selected NR values) instead of by content, and read with IFS= plus a delimiter that cannot be stripped.
needs_runtime_repro: Case (a): a [fixed] line with `$'\t'` at the end and an old fixed date. Run `found-issues archive` twice and count copies in the archive. Case (b): two identical [fixed] lines with `archive --count 1 --days 99999`; observe one archived and zero remaining.

summary: Auto-archive failures are swallowed: output is captured with `|| true` and printed only when it matches 'moved ... entries'.
failure_scenario: cmd_archive fails with 'could not compute cutoff date', or its mv or grep fail. The error text goes into archive_output and is discarded because it does not contain 'moved'. The explicit `sync` exits 0, and the user never learns that archiving is broken, so the ledger keeps growing.
evidence: lib/sync.sh:430 archive_output="$(cmd_archive 2>&1 || true)"; lib/sync.sh:432 if [[ "$archive_output" == *"moved"*"entries"* ]]; then
suggested_fix: Capture the exit status, and on non-zero print the captured text to stderr and return non-zero from sync.
needs_runtime_repro: Run explicit `sync` with `date` shadowed to fail, or with the ledger directory made read-only. Observe exit 0 and no message.

summary: sync and archive ignore merge-conflict markers, while fi_entries deliberately excludes conflict regions. sync flips entries inside both sides of a conflict, and archive removes lines from inside a conflict block.
failure_scenario: During a rebase or merge conflict in docs/found-issues.md (SessionStart still runs sync unattended), the `<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` regions stay in the file. sync processes `- [open]` lines inside them and may close one side. A later explicit archive, awk-matching `[fixed]` lines inside a region, moves one side's line to the archive and deletes it from the conflict.
